source_documents.title: Orthogonally Arranged π-Electronic Systems with Anion-Responsive Moiety Exhibiting Photoinduced Electron Transfer

reference_evidence_units.quote: suggesting that the electron transfer occurs in 2+ on a time scale of picoseconds and the generated electron-transferred state survives over nanosecond timescales.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Spectral evolution after the dpp local state, absent in less polar solvents, is assigned to ET.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Reported in a footnote; the radical bands are not assigned as explicitly as for 1, and the Cl- complex behaves unexpectedly.

reference_evidence_units.quote: These spectral evolutions were not observed in less polar solvents, especially in 2+ (Figure S22)
reference_evidence_units.statement: The evolution needs a polar solvent, as expected for charge separation.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: TA evolution from the dpp local state, absent in less polar solvents, is assigned to picosecond ET to the methylacridinium acceptor. Evidence is weaker than for 1 (footnote, less explicit band assignment).
